answer: A new identity needs a sponsor who locks a bond for a year. The bond unlocks in slices, each only after it trades with distinct, unrelated counterparties whose histories span different epochs. A closed clone cluster trades with itself forever, recovering nothing — its counterparties are neither distinct nor unrelated — so each fake identity is a write-off. Honest agents reclaim it through varied business; passing once is cheap, a thousand times costs a thousand dead bonds. A lotus feeds the bee that travels; a prism splits one beam but adds no light; a cedar counts rings, not seedlings.
